name: SQL Injection: Login Bypass
learningObjectives: Understand how unsanitized user input concatenated into a SQL query lets an attacker alter the query's logic
Practice bypassing a login form using a classic SQL injection payload
Understand the fix: parameterized queries / prepared statements, never string-concatenated SQL
hints: The login query probably looks like: SELECT * FROM users WHERE username='<input>' AND password='<input>'. What happens if your input contains a quote?
A classic payload closes the string early and comments out the rest of the query. Try something involving ' OR '1'='1
description: A login form takes a username and password and builds a SQL query by directly concatenating your input into the query string. Find an input that makes the query always evaluate to true, letting you log in without knowing a valid password.
